topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Data Movement
explanation: The memory hierarchy structures storage tiers (registers, L1/L2/L3 cache, main memory) to optimize the trade-off between access speed and capacity. Caching strategies govern the movement of data blocks, known as cache lines, between these levels. Data movement is primarily initiated by a CPU request; a cache miss triggers a block transfer from the slower, lower level to the faster, higher level. This transfer mechanism exploits spatial and temporal locality to ensure subsequent accesses hit the cache. Write policies, such as write-through or write-back, dictate when modified data is propagated down the hierarchy, maintaining coherence and minimizing effective memory access time.
